summary: Phoenix (proposal phoenix-ai-resilience-v1) meets the acceptance tests and bounded design constraints for resilient AI routing. It preserves provider/model lineage, excludes unavailable/errored providers from quorum, and maintains false safety flags. No votes are fabricated, and production behavior remains unchanged.
top_technical_reasons: Explicit timeout/error/rate-limit statuses ensure malformed or unavailable providers do not contribute to quorum.
Typed provider attempt records and short-prompt retry before fallback improve resilience without altering production weights.
Quorum is computed only from valid completed verdicts, excluding skipped, errored, or unavailable providers.
Safety flags (production_weights_changed, verdict_mutated) remain false, adhering to research-only constraints.
Fallback attempts preserve provider/model lineage, ensuring traceability of routing decisions.

next_experiments.hypothesis: Automating provider routing (beyond manual fallback) will reduce manual intervention without increasing timeout rates.
next_experiments.change: Implement dynamic provider selection based on real-time availability and performance metrics.
next_experiments.metric_gate: Timeout rate must not exceed 5% and quorum accuracy must remain at 100%.
next_experiments.why_it_is_informative: Validates whether automation improves resilience without compromising safety or increasing errors.

next_experiments.hypothesis: Short-prompt retry before fallback reduces malformed review rates without increasing latency.
next_experiments.change: Increase retry attempts for short prompts and measure impact on review quality and system responsiveness.
next_experiments.metric_gate: Malformed review rate must decrease by at least 20% and latency must not exceed 1.5x baseline.
next_experiments.why_it_is_informative: Determines if retry logic effectively mitigates malformed outputs while maintaining performance.

next_experiments.hypothesis: Excluding unavailable providers from quorum improves decision reliability without reducing approval rates.
next_experiments.change: Enforce quorum computation to strictly exclude providers marked as unavailable or errored.
next_experiments.metric_gate: Approval rate must remain within 95-105% of baseline, and error rate must not increase.
next_experiments.why_it_is_informative: Confirms that excluding unreliable providers does not harm decision quality or introduce bias.

data_or_label_risks.malformed_reviews: Recorded as errors but may indicate systemic issues in provider prompts or model outputs.
data_or_label_risks.timeout_handling: Timeouts are recorded but may mask underlying latency issues in provider infrastructure.
data_or_label_risks.quorum_exclusion: Excluding unavailable/errored providers could introduce bias if exclusion criteria are not representative.
data_or_label_risks.research_only_output: False production safety flags mean results are not validated for live deployment, limiting real-world risk assessment.
